news.title: Brad Friedel: World Cup won’t transform US soccer on its own
news.lede: Brad Fridal, former US and Premier League goalkeeper, knows better than most what it takes for an American player to succeed at football’s highest level. Friedel helped the United States reach the 2002 World Cup quarterfinals and spent nearly two decades in English football, including a then-record run of 310 consecutive Premier League appearances. Now, after another World Cup ended, with the US falling short of the last eight, Friedel believes the US’s failings aren’t within its funding or infrastructure. Instead, he believes the country must build a deeper football culture and warns that his own route to the Premier League might not even be possible for a young player today.

news.title: Qatar challenges AFC over open letter attacking FIFA President Infantino
news.lede: Oceania have offered support to Gianni Infantino, but New Zealand have gone against their own confederation in FIFA row. CAF have given under-fire Gianni Infantino their backing, and now say the FIFA president must stand in March’s election. Football’s top official boosted by further support for his presidency after proposed private investment in game nixed. Poland says their preparations to host the Women’s Under-20 World Cup remain on schedule, despite UEFA-FIFA fallout.

news.title: Oceania declares support for Infantino in boost for Fifa president but New Zealand breaks ranks
news.lede: OFC’s 11 votes could prove crucial in Fifa election. Stance shows continued backing from smaller nations. The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has declared its support for Gianni Infantino following demands from Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation for the Fifa president to resign, in a development that further highlights world football’s civil war. After a meeting of its executive committee in Fiji on Wednesday, the OFC issued a statement on Friday praising “the progress achieved over the last decade” by Fifa in its first public comments since the abandoned World Cup sell-off plan emerged this month.

news.title: Croatian football takeover underway in the United Arab Emirates
news.lede: The United Arab Emirates wants to reach the 2030 World Cup. To get there, it has turned to Croatia. As the UAE begins building towards the 2030 FIFA World Cup, it has placed its trust and gone all in on a group of coaches. Zlatko Dalić, Igor Bišćan and Branko Ivanković have all been appointed important roles, creating an unusually strong Croatian presence at the heart of the UAE’s football project.

news.title: Ghana clear major hurdle in bid to end 20-year World Cup absence
news.lede: Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens. Ghana's women's football team, the Black Queens, showed great courage to come from behind and defeat Côte d'Ivoire 2-1 in Casablanca. This victory keeps their dream of playing in the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup alive. The match started badly for Ghana.

news.title: Continental clash: where world football stands on Fifa and Infantino – explained
news.lede: With Oceania praising Fifa on Friday, all six confederations have finally had their say on the fallout from the World Cup sell-off plan. The Oceania Football Confederation’s (OFC) decision to belatedly issue a statement following this week’s executive committee meeting praising Fifa’s “progress achieved over the last decade” means all six continental confederations have finally had their say on the fallout from the World Cup sell-off plan that has split world football, with the votes seeming tied at three apiece on the key issue of whether Gianni Infantino should remain as Fifa president.
